title: Modification of the moving point test method for nighttime eddy CO2 flux filtering on hilly and complex terrains
author: Kang, Kim, et al.

steps.title: Select nighttime flux correction method
steps.instruction: Choose one of the three KoFlux nighttime correction methods (FVF, LRC, or modified VGF) and apply the site‑specific settings described below.

substeps.instruction: For the friction velocity filtering (FVF) method set the lower u* threshold to 0.3 m s⁻¹ for both GDK and GCK sites.

For the light‑response curve (LRC) method use the Michaelis‑Menten form NEE = RLRCd – (α Qt Amax)/(α Qt + Amax), where RLRCd is the estimated mean daytime ecosystem respiration obtained from regression of downward shortwave radiation versus daytime CO₂ flux.

For the modified van Gorsel (VGF) method compute the median diurnal variation of observed CO₂ flux for the chosen period, locate the sunset peak (Rmax), and use this peak directly as the threshold. Apply a 30‑day moving window to obtain daily RLRCd and Rmax.

steps.title: Fit temperature response function
steps.instruction: Estimate the Lloyd‑Taylor temperature response function (TRF) parameters for ecosystem respiration using the selected ER data.

substeps.instruction: Fit the equation ER = Rref · exp[ E0 · (1/Tref – 1/(Ta – T0)) ] where Tref = 10 °C, T0 = –46.02 °C, and Ta is the air temperature (°C).
Use a 30‑day moving window to estimate Rref; shift the window every 5 days to capture soil‑moisture and phenology effects.
Determine the activation energy E0 for each site‑year with the Reichstein et al. generic algorithm (E0 is held constant within a site‑year).

steps.title: Replace bad or missing ER data
steps.instruction: Substitute any missing or flagged ER values with those calculated from the fitted TRF using the corresponding air temperature.

steps.title: Filter nighttime flux outliers
steps.instruction: For the LRC and modified VGF methods, discard nighttime CO₂ flux observations that fall below the 95 % confidence interval of the fitted Lloyd‑Taylor ER model; do not filter daytime fluxes.

steps.title: Calculate GPP
steps.instruction: Compute gross primary production as GPP = NEE – ER for each time step.

steps.title: Define modified MPT time windows
steps.instruction: Create two night‑time windows based on the median diurnal CO₂ flux variation and the sunset peak.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the median diurnal variation of CO₂ flux over the analysis period and locate the time of the NEE peak (approximately sunset).
First window: from one hour before to two hours after the identified peak time (‑1 h to +2 h).
Second window: the remaining night period immediately following the first window.

steps.title: Apply original MPT to each window
steps.instruction: Run the moving point test algorithm separately for the first and second windows to obtain lower and upper u* thresholds.

substeps.instruction: Initialize outer‑loop thresholds: u*L = 0, u*H = 9999.
Derive the TRF (Lloyd‑Taylor) using data whose u* values lie between u*L and u*H.
Normalize each CO₂ flux by dividing the measured flux by the TRF‑predicted flux.
Remove outliers with the 3σ rule and sort the remaining data by ascending u*.
Initialize inner‑loop thresholds: u*L = 0, u*H = 9999.
Starting from the highest u* value, take n = 25 consecutive points (moving sample).
Perform a two‑sample t‑test (significance level αMPT = 0.1) comparing the mean normalized flux of the moving sample (Fm) to the mean of the reference sample (Fr).
If H0 (Fm ≠ Fr) is rejected, shift the moving sample to the next lower‑u* group and repeat the t‑test.
If H0 is not rejected, set the median u* of the moving sample as the new u*L (or, if this occurs on the first test, as the new u*H).
Whenever u*L or u*H is updated, return to the outer‑loop step 2 and iterate until the final test rejects H0; the last updated u*L and u*H are the thresholds for that window.

steps.title: Assess drainage significance between windows
steps.instruction: Compare the mean normalized nighttime CO₂ fluxes of the two windows to decide whether drainage at midnight is significant.

substeps.instruction: Perform a statistical test (e.g., t‑test) on the two window means.
If the means differ significantly, consider drainage significant and discard all data from the second window.

steps.title: Apply friction velocity filtering with MPT thresholds
steps.instruction: Using the u*L and u*H obtained from the modified MPT, filter nighttime CO₂ fluxes in both windows with the friction velocity (FVF) method.

substeps.instruction: Retain only data with u* ≥ u*L and u* ≤ u*H for each window.
Proceed with downstream analyses (e.g., flux partitioning, GPP calculation) using the filtered dataset.
